title: Cross with YHWH letters beside Passover doorway, both marked with blood
summary: Two drawings side by side with no sentences: on the left a tan wooden cross with the four Hebrew letters י ה ו ה running down its upright beam and red blood smears at the top, both arm ends and the base; on the right a Passover door frame with blood on the lintel, both doorposts and the threshold. The slide visually links the blood on the cross with the blood on the doorposts.

words.gloss: the name of God (the four letters on the cross)

letters.meaning: first letter of YHWH, drawn in maroon at the top of the cross
second letter of YHWH, drawn in black across the cross beam
third letter of YHWH, drawn in orange on the upright beam
fourth letter of YHWH, drawn in black near the base of the cross

pictures.description: Simple flat drawing of a tan wooden cross with scribbled red blood marks at the top, at the ends of both arms and on the lower upright beam. The Hebrew letters yod (maroon), he (black), vav (orange) and he (black) are laid down the upright beam, spelling YHWH.

Simple flat drawing of a golden-brown wooden door frame with a darker brown door swung open, an orange doorknob, and scribbled red blood smears on the lintel, on both doorposts and on the ground at the threshold.

uncertain: The slide has no words explaining the pairing; the summary only describes what is drawn.
The red scribbles on the cross and door are read as blood smears.
